item.title: Neural Realized Measures: Forecast-Supervised Intraday Aggregation for Volatility Forecasting
item.content:encoded:
高频波动率预测, 神经实现测度, 预测监督聚合, 实现测度, 加密货币

总结: 文章提出Neural Realized Measures (NRM)框架，通过预测目标监督学习聚合权重，替代传统固定规则。该方法保留了原始测度贡献及逐条目归因能力，且包含传统方法作为特例。在Heston模拟和加密货币数据的评估中，NRM在多种模型下均降低了RMSE和QLIKE。分析显示学习到的权重具有系统性的时间效应和非线性上下文特征。
High-frequency volatility forecasting typically separates measurement from prediction: intraday observations are first compressed into a daily realized measure using a fixed aggregation rule, and the resulting statistic is then passed to a forecasting model. This conventional pipeline therefore treats measure construction as forecast-agnostic preprocessing. We ask whether the aggregation stage itself can instead be learned from the downstream forecasting objective while preserving the statistical structure of established realized measures. We propose Neural Realized Measures (NRM), a primitive-preserving, forecast-supervised aggregation framework that retains the original measure-specific intraday contributions but replaces uniform aggregation with positive, mean-normalized context-dependent weights. Uniform weights exactly recover the corresponding raw realized measure (RRM), so the classical construction is nested as a special case. Because NRM remains an explicit weighted sum of established primitive contributions, it also retains direct bar-level attribution. Across SF, HAR, and MIDAS forecasting specifications, NRM is evaluated against corresponding RRM specifications under controlled comparisons. In Heston simulations, NRM reduces RMSE for both contemporaneous and next-day latent integrated variance across all evaluated primitive--regime combinations. On six cryptocurrencies using five-minute data, NRM improves QLIKE in all 54 paired out-of-sample comparisons, with mean gains of 7.23\%, 8.15\%, and 9.22\% under SF, HAR, and MIDAS, respectively. Validation-selected NRM specifications also achieve the lowest mean QLIKE across the six assets among the evaluated approaches. Ablation and SHAP analyses reveal systematic time-of-day and nonlinear local-context effects in the learned allocation. arXiv categories: q-fin.ST, stat.ML

item.title: A general technique for explicit quantile representations
item.content:encoded:
分位数积分 解析密度 独立性 Black-Scholes隐含波动率 区间表示

总结: 本文证明了严格正实解析密度的分位数积分存在独立于概率水平的轮廓。文章提供了明确的构造方法，覆盖了五个广泛的分布族。最终，利用前向函数得出了Black-Scholes隐含波动率的有限区间表示。
This work proves existence of contours independent of probability level for exact quantile integrals of strictly positive real-analytic densities. Explicit constructions cover five broad distribution families and yield a finite-interval representation of Black-Scholes implied volatility using forward functions. arXiv categories: q-fin.ST, math.PR

item.title: Beyond Anonymous Order Flow: Wallet Identity as a Feature for Short-Horizon Return Prediction
item.content:encoded:
Hyperliquid, Level-4, 钱包身份, 回报预测, 高频交易特征

总结: 本文利用Hyperliquid Level-4数据（含钱包身份）重构全深度订单簿，进行短期回报预测。研究发现，基于名义交易量的排名在相邻窗口间保持稳定。通过将钱包身份作为特征，在调整协变量后，预测收益在顶部十分位达到3.11个基点。此外，利用顶级交易者的特征将1秒期外R2从10.88%提升至12%。
Conventional public order-book data summarize trading without identifying the accounts behind it. Hyperliquid's Level-4 record also exposes persistent pseudonymous wallet addresses. We reconstruct full-depth books from consensus-ordered messages and evaluate wallet identity as a feature for short-horizon return prediction. The July 1-27, 2026 record covers 17.1 billion messages, 14.3 million aggressive orders by 147,113 wallets, and $84.3 billion in taker notional across ten markets. In the three model markets, notional-weighted ten-second markout rankings persist across adjacent ten-day windows (Spearman rho = 0.52); covariate-adjusted validation markouts reach 3.11 basis points in the top ventile. On a 100-millisecond grid, eleven features describing previously scored top-decile wallets raise one-second out-of-sample R2 from 10.88% to 12. arXiv categories: q-fin.TR, q-fin.ST

item.title: Aggregate Calibration Can Mask Stress-State Undercoverage: Bounded-Memory Forecast Intervals under Recurrent Financial Stress
item.content:encoded:
序列预测区间, 校准记忆限制, 高波动状态, 金融范围预测, 近期优先

总结: 1. **问题识别**：序列预测区间仅靠聚合覆盖率评估会受限于校准记忆，导致在经济重要状态复发后出现误导。
2. **实验设置**：在次日金融范围预测中，保持模型和预算不变，对比了近期优先（FIFO）、无界状态历史和罕见重放三种方法。
3. **实证结果**：近期优先校准虽整体达标，但在高波动状态期间严重覆盖不足；罕见重放方法在高VIX区间表现更优。
4. **核心结论**：有界校准记忆属于预测信息设计，仅凭聚合校准指标无法发现特定状态下的可靠性失败。
Sequential forecast intervals are often evaluated by aggregate coverage even when calibration memory is bounded. This can be misleading when economically important states recur after long absences: a recent-only buffer may satisfy its overall coverage target while no longer containing errors from earlier episodes of the returning state. We study this problem in next-day financial range forecasting, holding the forecasting model, conformity score, adaptive update, and memory budget constant while varying the historical residual information available at each query. Recent-only first-in, first-out (FIFO) calibration is near nominal in aggregate but undercovers substantially during high-volatility states in both an exchange-traded fund development panel and a fixed stock panel. An unbounded state-history reference yields a lower observed stress-period interval score; Rare replay yields lower high-VIX interval scores than the matched Recent-n and Hybrid-n controls in both panels, and the state-structured versus recent-only contrast is largest near stress re-entry. Bounded calibration memory is therefore part of the forecasting information design, and aggregate calibration alone can conceal state-specific reliability failures. arXiv categories: stat.ME, q-fin.ST

item.title: Decomposing Rank Reversals under Temporal Nonstationarity: Alignment, Aggressiveness, and Instability
item.content:encoded:
时间非平稳性、模型排名逆转、R方分解、记忆敏感度、自适应回溯

总结:
提出统一框架：针对时间非平稳性下模型排名逆转问题，建立统一理论框架。
将预测误差分解为对齐度、失准激进性和预测不稳定性。
理论推导：推导复杂度边界，给出局部漂移下岭回归的最优记忆方程。
机制验证：在金融数据上验证，证明排名逆转由激进性激增驱动。
Under temporal nonstationarity, model performance rankings reverse across training horizons due to heterogeneous sensitivities to memory. While existing literature addresses adaptive lookbacks, effective model complexity, and empirical forecast evaluation in isolation, no unified framework explains the structural mechanics driving these rank reversals. We bridge this gap by deriving a model-agnostic decomposition of out-of-sample $R^2$ into target alignment, miscalibrated aggressiveness, and predictive instability. Within this framework, we mathematically characterize complexity phase boundaries, establish closed-form optimal-memory equations for ridge regression under local drift, and extend these guarantees to complex model architectures via surrogate bounds. We validate these theoretical dynamics by benchmarking 14 linear, tree-based, and neural architectures across large-scale financial panels. In doing so, our framework demonstrates that empirical model rank reversals are driven by predictable surges in miscalibrated aggressiveness, providing a rigorous mechanistic diagnosis of generalization under temporal shift. arXiv categories: cs.LG, q-fin.ST

item.title: Are LLM Research Agents Reliable Judges of Predictability? Evidence from Planted-Signal Worlds
item.content:encoded:
Researchers ask large language model (LLM) research agents whether a forecasting model beats a static benchmark, a verdict that real data cannot check. We treat the agent as a statistical test and score pre-specified runs of three frontier models and one open-weight model in simulated worlds with a planted signal. The agents detect weak signals more often than a pre-specified out-of-sample test, mainly because they accept weaker evidence: held to an agent's false-positive rate, a conventional in-sample test does as well or better. The agents claim predictability too often in worlds without a signal, state miscalibrated probabilities, and change their verdicts after a sentence about prior research; the magnitudes depend on the model. The excess false claims persist in simulated worlds without a resampling artifact. Agent verdicts are informative but need a neutral brief, a decision rule fixed outside the agent and a sealed holdout.
arXiv categories: q-fin.ST

item.title: PanelGP: A Probabilistic Factor Model for Asset-Return Panels
item.content:encoded:
PanelGP, 高斯过程, 条件因子模型, 非参数估计, 股票回报

总结: 1. 提出PanelGP，利用高斯过程非参数估计公司特征与经济条件对因子载荷及期望因子的影响。 2. 通过稀疏变分推断分离异质与系统性风险，并预测回报和协方差矩阵。 3. 相比IPCAs，非线性载荷能更好排名股票并提升预测准确度。 4. 实证显示投资组合具有更高夏普比率和更低波动率。 5. 但预测方差对风险的区分度不足，存在过度压缩现象。
We develop PanelGP, a conditional factor model for large panels of stock returns in which firm characteristics determine the factor loadings and economic conditions determine the expected factors. Both relations are estimated nonparametrically with Gaussian-process priors. The kernel choice nests instrumented principal component analysis (IPCA) as well as smooth nonlinear maps. Asset-specific loading innovations and common factor innovations separate idiosyncratic from systematic risk, so one estimated model forecasts both expected returns and their covariance matrix. Estimation uses sparse variational inference with a joint posterior over loadings and factors. Because each predicted return is bilinear in a Gaussian state, the predictive covariance matrix and the cumulants of any portfolio have closed forms. In simulations, the estimator recovers the nonlinear maps and the variance parameters. For S&P 500 constituents over 1995-2024, nonlinear loadings rank stocks better than affine loadings and improve the Gaussian log score. Relative to IPCA, the resulting portfolios have higher Sharpe ratios, also net of trading costs, and the minimum-variance portfolio has lower volatility. The predicted variances rank stocks and months by risk but are too compressed. arXiv categories: q-fin.ST, econ.EM, stat.ML

item.title: Thinking Fast, Trading Late: System One Decision Models vs the Market
item.content:encoded:
大语言模型, 股票预测, OLIVIA协议, 稳健性测试, 信息系数

总结: 1. 大语言模型通过阅读新闻预测股票，但需严格测试排除过拟合。 2. 提出OLIVIA协议，通过掩码身份和加密分析计划进行盲测。 3. 实验显示，微调模型在盲测中信号减弱，商业模型仅能预测开盘价变动。 4. 没有策略能盈利，且模型能识别被掩码的公司，表明市场先于模型知晓新闻。
Large language models (LLMs) read company news at scale, and backtests suggest that their readings predict stock returns. We ask how much of that predictability survives a test that rules out look-ahead, memorization and selection. We propose OLIVIA, a protocol for such tests: point-in-time inputs with company identities masked, selection on validation data only, an analysis plan frozen by cryptographic hash, and a test period unblinded once through a logged lock. We apply it to AI decision models, non-generative language models that return probabilities for typed questions, reading news about S&P 500 stocks: an open-weights model we fine-tuned on 2024-2025 data, three commercial models and standard baselines. The fine-tuned model's signal replicated on two validation quarters (daily information coefficients 0.055 and 0.065) but fell to 0.020 (t = 1.7) on the blinded January-July 2026 test. The commercial models' readings line up with the overnight move to the open (information coefficient 0.074 to 0.077) but not with the move after it, so the news is priced by the time a trader can act on it at the open. No model can tell over- from under-reaction, and no pre-registered strategy survives costs and a deflated Sharpe ratio. Commercial models identify masked companies in 62% to 74% of cases against a 28% baseline: masking hides names, not companies. The market reads the news first. arXiv categories: cs.AI, cs.CL, cs.LG, q-fin.ST

item.title: Hardware-Aware Design and Layout Selection in Quantum Reservoir Computing for Insurance Claims Forecasting
item.content:encoded:
量子储备池计算, 保险索赔预测, 硬件感知布局, IBM Kingston, 转移鲁棒性

总结: 文章验证了小型量子储备池计算（QRC）在预测次日汽车保险索赔中的竞争力。通过基于硬件本原图和动力学筛选出五个候选模型，理想模拟中其RMSE与经典Ridge回归相当。在IBM Kingston处理器上，采用硬件感知布局显著优于Qiskit布局，避免了随机布局的严重失败，并将最大转移失真控制在7.59（Qiskit为11.84）。文章发现硬件感知布局能有效减少系统性预报偏移，结论是小型QRC能达到竞争性精度，且硬件感知布局能确保向硬件的稳定转移。
Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) processes temporal information through quantum dynamics, but it remains unclear whether small QRC models can forecast real data competitively with classical models and whether their predictions survive the transfer from ideal simulation to noisy hardware. We address both questions for a six-qubit gate-based reservoir that forecasts next-day motor-insurance claim counts. Five reservoir candidates were selected and frozen using hardware-native interaction graphs, Trotterized Ising dynamics, memory and measurement-robustness criteria, circuit cost, and calibrated-noise screening. On 232 held-out test days, the ideal candidates reached root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) of 5.66-6.12 claims/day, compared with 5.36 for ridge regression. For four of the five, the difference from ridge was not significant under a 95% block bootstrap, and their accuracy was comparable with classical recurrent and reservoir baselines. On the 156-qubit IBM Kingston processor, we ran 63 evaluations in 21 paired rounds, comparing hardware-aware, random-native, and Qiskit optimization level 1 layouts. Hardware-aware placement gave lower RMSE than Qiskit in every round, with a maximum transfer distortion of 7.59 claims/day (11.84 for Qiskit), and avoided the severe transfer failures seen for some random layouts. Most of the hardware distortion appeared as a systematic forecast shift, which a short hardware probe on training inputs detected before the test runs. Longer replay windows raised circuit cost without a consistent gain in forecasting accuracy or hardware transfer. Small QRC models can thus reach competitive accuracy on this task, and hardware-aware layout selection makes their transfer to IBM Kingston more consistent. arXiv categories: quant-ph, cs.LG, q-fin.ST

item.title: Can We Stop the Backtest Yet? Anytime-Valid Promotion Tests for Adaptive Financial Research Agents
item.content:encoded:
PROMOTE协议 交易规则 财富分配 Ville论证 伪外样本回放

总结: 文章提出了 PROMOTE 协议，为候选交易规则分配可预测的测试财富，并仅从回报中积累成本感知的 e-process。基于加权 Ville 论证，该协议在总财富约束下限制了宣称净得分非正的规则被推广的概率，支持依赖性候选和自适应监控。实验表明，相比未调整测试，PROMOTE 在零假设路径上实现了零假阳性，且具备 70.1% 的目标功率。市场回放显示成本后无推广。需注意，该证书仅控制历史错误推广，不保证部署时的盈利能力。
Financial research agents can generate and monitor trading rules faster than a human can document the resulting selection process. Candidates appear at data-dependent times, weak rules are abandoned, and promising ones are watched until they cross a reporting threshold. We introduce PROMOTE, a protocol that assigns every candidate predictable testing wealth at birth and accumulates a cost-aware e-process only from subsequent returns. If lifetime allocations sum to at most one, a weighted Ville argument bounds the probability of ever promoting a rule whose declared bounded net score has always had nonpositive conditional mean. The result permits dependent candidates, adaptive births, and indefinite monitoring. We audit the implementation in two settings. A retrospective pseudo-out-of-sample replay contains 24 panel--rule hypotheses, 3,000 shared-sign null paths, injected alternatives, and public ETF and industry data. Repeated unadjusted tests produce a family crossing in 94.5% of null paths, versus 0.0% for PROMOTE; at a 15-bp aligned ETF-component perturbation, PROMOTE has 70.1% target power and median crossing session 2,327. A separate exact mean-zero experiment lets an agent select candidate identities and birth times from past scores; the funded gate has 1.77% false-family crossings across 3,000 programs. The market replay produces zero promotions after costs. The certificate controls historical false promotion under the declared null; it is not a certificate that an earlier edge remains profitable at deployment. AI-use disclosure. Generative AI tools, including OpenAI Codex, assisted manuscript preparation. For this preprint version, Codex assisted with LaTeX editing, author and venue metadata, compilation, and layout checks. arXiv categories: cs.AI, q-fin.ST

item.title: EventGPT: Next-Event Pretraining on Banking Customer Histories
item.content:encoded:
EventGPT 银行事件预测 分层因果Transformer 无监督预训练 下游任务

总结:EventGPT是一种用于预测客户下一个事件的分层因果Transformer。它在包含千万级交易和定位数据的数据集上进行无监督预训练，训练效率高。模型在无标签情况下对首次交易等目标的预测准确率高达0.92，优于需大量标注数据的梯度提升方法。在产品预测任务中，其冻结嵌入虽略逊于工程特征，但作为集成组件能提升性能。代码与权重已开源。
A model pretrained to predict a customer's next event can estimate the probability of future events without training on their labels and provide a reusable representation for supervised downstream banking tasks. We pretrain EventGPT, a hierarchical causal transformer, by next-token maximum likelihood estimation on the public Multimodal Banking Dataset (MBD-mini: 100,224 clients, 38.8 million transactions and 66.3 million geolocation pings). Keeping one state per event, EventGPT trains in about two hours on one L4 GPU at windows up to 8,192 tokens. From its next-event distribution, with no labels, EventGPT scores five targets of the form "the client makes a transaction of a given kind for the first time next month" at ROC-AUC 0.79 to 0.92. Gradient boosting on 114 engineered features needs 10,000 to 300,000 labeled client-months to match it on four targets and stays below it on the fifth. For product prediction, frozen EventGPT embeddings score below the engineered features (mean ROC-AUC 0.787 against 0.808 over five test folds), and a rank-averaged ensemble of EventGPT, profile fields and token counts with the engineered features adds 0.014 to 0.017, of which 0.007 to 0.016 is EventGPT's own. The code and pretrained weights are released. arXiv categories: stat.ML, cs.LG, q-fin.ST

item.title: Honest Small Decision Models for Finance: Scale, Specialization Collapse, and Mixed-Corpus Remediation
item.content:encoded:
System-1决策模型, 金融校准, 窄域微调, 混合语料补救, 概率预测

总结: 本文针对金融工作流提出System-1决策模型，在K2-Horizon和Qwen系列上验证了0.8B至32B参数模型。研究发现窄域微调会损害通用决策能力，且模型在现实结果问题上表现自然诚实的平坦校准概率。通过混合语料补救，可在保持政策天花板和校准的同时，提升公开基准表现，实现部署。
Financial workflows need fast, calibrated, auditable decisions, not just generated text. We train System-1 decision models, small language models fine-tuned to answer typed questions (choice/score/noul) with a probability in a single forward pass, across two model families (K2-Horizon and Qwen3.5/3.8) and nine rungs from 0.8B to 32B parameters, using one frozen LoRA recipe on a public decision benchmark and two new finance corpora: a programmatic-gold policy corpus (rule-reading with exact labels) and a reality-labeled outcome corpus (19,640 realized forward-return questions in walk-forward splits, plus a sealed 2026 test of 1,360 questions). Narrow fine-tuning costs general decision competence 9-45 percentage points, a data-mixture effect that shrinks with model scale and is associated with narrow-gradient volume. On reality-labeled questions, every trained rung from 0.8B to 32B lands at the horizon-conditioned prior baseline (accuracy 0.37-0.38, no detectable conditional edge under our controls); the models respond with flat, well-calibrated probabilities that track per-horizon base rates: naturally honest uncertainty, with a mid-scale calibration sweet spot (ECE 0.026 at 2B, degrading to 0.043-0.044 at 9-32B under prior drift). A mixed-corpus remediation carries all competencies in one adapter at modest cost: it matches or slightly exceeds the generalist specialist on the public benchmark while holding the policy ceiling and near-specialist outcome calibration, yielding a deployable artifact with per-domain temperature regimes and a band-dispatch escalation analysis: sharp, dispatchable bands where rules determine answers; flat, review-routing bands where reality does not. arXiv categories: cs.LG, q-fin.ST

item.title: TensorLOB: Structure-Preserving Tensor Learning for Limit Order Book Forecasting
item.content:encoded:
The limit order book (LOB) records outstanding buy and sell orders across multiple price levels. Its state evolves over time across market side, price level, and order attribute, naturally forming a multiway structure. However, existing LOB models typically flatten these dimensions into a matrix model, thus obscuring the existing structural relationships. Starting from first principles and the market-microstructure intuition of the LOB, we design TensorLOB to operate entirely in the tensor domain. TensorLOB uses mode-wise tensor contractions for feature extraction and directly contracts the learned representation with low-rank class-weight tensors for prediction, retaining the distinct roles of time, side, level, and attribute modes. Experiments on the FI-2010 benchmark show that TensorLOB achieves the highest accuracy, recall, and F1 score across all four evaluated horizons. This proof of concept highlights the potential of high-dimensional modelling of multi-way latent information intrinsic to financial markets, which has so far been largely overlooked.
arXiv categories: cs.LG, q-fin.ST

item.title: Boom-Busty Marketron as a Model of Market Dynamics: How Investor-Market Reflexivity Amplifies Non-Equilibrium
item.content:encoded:
We introduce the Boom-Busty Marketron, a model of a multi-asset market in which the demand of a single collective investor moves prices and itself depends on market performance. This creates an investor-market reflexive loop in the spirit of Soros's theory. The market state is stationary without being at equilibrium: a non-equilibrium steady state (NESS), with broken detailed balance and a probability current circulating between mispricing, demand and volatility. While stochastic volatility with the leverage effect already breaks detailed balance and makes the market dynamics irreversible, the investor-market loop pushes the market further away from equilibrium. Calibrated to the S\&P 500 from 1996 to 2024 by simulated moments, the model reproduces the stylised facts of returns together with quantitative metrics of the market, including cross-sectional ones, and its return and cycle statistics stay stationary for a century and a half on the 1996--2010 inputs. Its central emergent behaviour is a boom-bust cycle, whose frequency meets the S\&P's within one-sigma ranges. The model also produces a default rate of the order of that of investment-grade issuers, prices inside Fisher Black's factor of two of value, the dumb-money effect of Frazzini and Lamont, and a measurable arrow of time. Standard long-short factors built from its cross section rotate through the cycle, and so do its industry groups along the defensive axis.
arXiv categories: q-fin.ST, nlin.AO, q-fin.GN

item.title: Do Round Numbers Hold Prices? Occupation Densities and Depth-Conditioned Hazards in the Limit Order Book
item.content:encoded:
价格聚类, 限价订单簿, Tick网格框架, 深度调整持续时间, 流动性

总结:文章利用Tick网格框架分析限价订单簿数据，探讨了价格聚集现象。
1. 研究发现圆整水平确实吸引更多流动性。
2. 但深度调整持续时间在圆整水平并无显著差异。
3. Intel和SoFi显示出方向性效应，价格倾向于离开圆整水平。
Prices cluster at round numbers, a pattern often interpreted as evidence that these levels act as price barriers. This pattern also admits a mechanical explanation: more liquidity rests there, and prices take longer to leave deeper queues. Limit order book data allow us to distinguish these mechanisms through a tick-grid framework in which local time counts departures and level-wise volatility reflects the departure hazard. Using data for five Nasdaq stocks throughout 2025, we find that round levels attract more liquidity but do not exhibit longer depth-adjusted durations. Intel and SoFi show directional effects, with departures biased away from round levels. arXiv categories: q-fin.TR, q-fin.ST

item.title: Compiling and forecasting implied volatility surfaces via survey sampling, tempered inverse-probability sequence learning, and causal activity clocks
item.content:encoded:
隐含波动率, 有限总体抽样, LSTM, 非平稳性, 预测能力

总结: 本文基于2018-2025年NVDA数据，研究IV曲面与风险预测。一是IV曲面重建中，基于滞后离散度的分层插值优于PPS；二是LSTM训练中，PPS和Neyman设计比SRS保留更多尾部窗口，虽节省时间但增量收益不明显；三是短期价格不可预测，远期IV仅具均值回归技能且未胜过HAR-IV；四是在价格大幅扩张期间，滚动量和美元时钟稳定了条形率并压缩了日内回报峰度。
Compiling implied volatility (IV) surfaces and forecasting derivative risk from high-frequency equity and options feeds requires addressing contract heterogeneity, schema shifts, volatility clustering, and non-stationary trading activity. Using a split-adjusted NVIDIA (NVDA) equity and options panel (2018-2025), this study integrates finite-population survey sampling, tempered inverse-probability sequence learning, and causal activity clocks. Four findings emerge. First, cross-sectional surface accuracy depends on matching the sampling design to the target functional: plug-in stratified allocations using lagged cell dispersion improve equal-weighted surface reconstruction with full grid coverage, whereas liquidity-weighted probability proportional to size (PPS) sampling excels on liquidity-weighted targets by construction yet inflates error when misapplied. Second, in longitudinal LSTM sequence training, PPS and Neyman designs retain more tail-volatility windows than simple random sampling (SRS); all three designs are equivalent to full-census training within chosen margins while cutting training time, though incremental forecasting gains of informative selection over SRS are not established. Third, out-of-sample evaluation shows a predictability contrast: short-horizon prices are not forecastable beyond a random walk with drift among tested models, whereas forward IV shows descriptive mean-reversion skill concentrated in a few post-shock reversal sessions (insignificant under session-clustered tests), with sequence models not beating a linear HAR-IV benchmark and feature pruning driving stability. Fourth, across a 6.3x start-to-end (nearly twentyfold trough-to-peak) price expansion, rolling volume and dollar clocks stabilize bar rates and compress intraday return kurtosis beyond diurnal scaling. arXiv categories: stat.AP, q-fin.ST

item.title: Sparse Autoencoders as Implicit Diversification Regularisers for Cross-Sectional Cryptocurrency Returns
item.content:encoded:
Sparse Autoencoder, Cryptocurrency Returns, Portfolio Diversification, Low Volatility, Factor Stability

总结: 本文利用稀疏自编码器（SAE）提取金融因子以解决神经因子解释性差及风险不明的问题。研究发现SAE投资组合具有较低波动性，体现了资产间的低相关性，从而支持了投资组合的分散化。然而，SAE并未在风险调整后收益上超越简单的反向策略，且其因子身份在训练中不稳定。本文的贡献在于明确将这种分散化效应与关于Alpha或因子稳定性的主张区分开来。
Factor models are central to asset pricing and portfolio construction, but neural factors are often difficult to interpret, and their effect on portfolio risk is unclear. A sparse autoencoder (SAE) may address both concerns by describing daily returns across many assets with only a few active features. We ask whether this sparse representation produces stable financial factors and better-diversified portfolios. We study cryptocurrency returns, use equities as a secondary test, and compare the SAE with common benchmarks in a time-ordered evaluation. We find consistently lower volatility in SAE portfolios and link this result to lower correlations among the selected assets. However, the SAE does not outperform a simple contrarian strategy on risk-adjusted return, and its factor identities are not stable across training runs. Our contribution is to show that sparse coding can support portfolio diversification, while clearly separating this risk effect from claims about alpha or stable factor identities. arXiv categories: cs.LG, q-fin.PM, q-fin.ST

item.title: Calibration of Passive Market Impact with a Queue-Sensitive Propagator Model
item.content:encoded:
被动市场影响, Hawkes模型, 价格分解, 订单流失衡, 微观结构

总结: 本文提出被动市场影响框架，基于Hawkes驱动的订单流与队列反应模型。研究发现价格分解为通用传播项和依赖于最佳报价成交量的状态依赖修正项。通过回归可观测信号（传播信号与队列加权订单流失衡）进行校准。结果表明，被动影响项显著解释了价格变化，优于经典模型，提升了拟合度和预测精度。
We develop a framework for calibrating passive market impact, defined as the price response to liquidity-providing limit orders, in contrast to the impact of liquidity-consuming market orders. We build on the model of Ouazzani Chahdi, Rosenbaum, and Szymanski (arxiv:2412.07461), which combines Hawkes-driven market-order flow with queue-reactive limit-order and cancellation dynamics. Within this model, we show that the price decomposes into a universal propagator term driven by signed order-flow imbalance and a state-dependent correction that captures the dependence of price sensitivity on volume at the best quotes. This decomposition links limit-order-book microstructure to standard propagator models and yields a regression on two observable signals: the propagator signal and the queue-weighted order-flow imbalance. We calibrate the model on high-frequency order-book data and find that the passive-impact term explains substantial variation in prices beyond the classical propagator, improving both model fit and the accuracy of predicted impact curves. arXiv categories: q-fin.TR, math.PR, q-fin.MF, q-fin.ST

item.title: Contemporaneous Transmission Networks and Systemic Risk in European Banking
item.content:encoded:
欧洲银行, 系统性暴露, 递归非高斯网络, 传导效应, 风险评分

总结: 1. 本文研究了欧洲银行的系统性暴露，利用递归非高斯网络模型构建了基于市值加权的系统性影响评分（SIS）和系统性脆弱性评分（SVS）。 2. 研究揭示了银行间不同的传导与接收角色，发现接收角色比传导角色更具可重复性。 3. 波动率标准化降低了检测到的依赖性，但全样本模型未满足独立性标准，且排序选择影响结果。 4. 结论提供了关注不确定性的互补风险度量。
We study how contemporaneous equity-return transmission shapes systemic exposure among 51 listed European banks. Using a recursive non-Gaussian network model on volatility-standardized returns, we construct two market-capitalization-weighted measures based on direct and indirect transmission effects: the Systemic Impact Score (SIS), capturing a bank's potential influence on other institutions, and the Systemic Vulnerability Score (SVS), capturing its exposure to disturbances originating elsewhere. The fitted network reveals distinct transmitting and receiving roles, highlighting differences between institutions with substantial outward influence and those with high incoming sensitivity. Receiving roles are generally more reproducible than transmitting roles across repeated network discovery, and selected connections remain informative about lower-tail dependence in subsequent observations. Volatility standardization substantially reduces detected dependence among recovered shocks, although the full-sample model does not satisfy the designated criterion for supporting shock independence. Alternative recursive orderings also yield comparable directional tail asymmetries, limiting the extent to which these patterns validate a particular ordering. The results provide complementary measures of model-implied systemic transmission and vulnerability, with explicit attention to uncertainty and identification limits arXiv categories: q-fin.ST, econ.EM

item.title: Event definition and the branching ratio: Hawkes estimates of price-change clustering in the consolidated quote feed
item.content:encoded:
Hawkes模型, 价格变化, 亚毫秒级核组件, NBBO, 报价源

总结: * Hawkes模型在分析价格变化时发现了亚毫秒级核组件和临界分支比。 * 在大额报价股票中，该组件源于NBBO报价源的构造，其中一半的变化是锁单或报价耗尽，在1毫秒内解决。 * 将事件定义为持续1毫秒的中间价格可移除此组件；原始拟合显示1秒内有3倍核质量，模拟结果证实了这一点。 * 由于分支比与基准线权衡，核质量在固定窗口上报告。
Hawkes models of price changes in the consolidated US quote feed find a sub-millisecond kernel component and a branching ratio near criticality. We show that in large-tick stocks the first is the feed's construction: half of NBBO changes are locks or depleted quotes, resolved within a millisecond, which the model reads as excitation. Defining the event as a mid-price level persisting for one millisecond removes the component. Raw fits put three times the clean kernel mass within one second, which a simulation reproduces. Since the total branching ratio trades off against the baseline, we report kernel mass on a fixed window. arXiv categories: q-fin.ST, q-fin.CP, q-fin.TR

item.title: FinLLM-KG: Knowledge Graph-Enhanced LLMs for Financial Sentiment Analysis in Algorithmic Trading
item.content:encoded:
Financial Sentiment Analysis, Causal LLMs, Knowledge Graph, Explainability, FinLLM-KG

总结: 现有金融情感分析孤立预测且是黑盒。为此，提出FinLLM-KG框架，结合因果LLM与金融知识图谱。该方法在推理时注入SEC 10-K的公司级知识，无需更新权重且计算成本低。通过归因机制增强了可解释性。模拟表明，该框架持续优于最先进基线，提升了投资组合表现。
Recent advances in Generative AI have substantially improved financial sentiment analysis through post-trained financial large language models (LLMs). However, existing approaches remain confined to predicting the sentiment of each article in isolation and operate as black boxes, which limits contextual understanding and hinders deployment in high-stakes financial decision-making. To this end, we introduce FinLLM-KG, a model-agnostic framework that combines causal LLMs with a financial knowledge graph, in order to inject temporally grounded, company-level knowledge from SEC 10-K filings at inference time, without updating model weights. Within FinLLM-KG, context is supplied either as a natural-language company profile or as a small set of relevance-ranked factual triples. This enables sentiment predictions to account for broader firm-level information rather than the article alone, at almost zero computational cost and for any causal LLM. In addition, attributing each article-level sentiment score to individual sentences and to the retrieved knowledge-graph facts makes the evidence behind the prediction inspectable, thereby enhancing explainability and supporting human-in-the-loop review. Simulations demonstrate that FinLLM-KG consistently improves portfolio performance over the state-of-the-art baseline. arXiv categories: cs.CL, cs.LG, q-fin.ST, q-fin.TR

item.title: Weekend Crypto Volatility and Monday Market Risk
item.content:encoded:
加密货币 周末波动率 周一方差 异质自回归模型 ETF批准

总结: 1. 研究考察了周末加密货币波动率对周一股票、大宗商品及固定收益市场方差的影响。 2. 利用2017-2026数据，在异质自回归模型中引入共同周末因子，发现2024年后预测内容显著增强。 3. 周末因子变动与周一方差显著正相关，能降低预测损失，且优于周五波动率及币种特异性信息。 4. 突变点估计在2023年底受现货比特币ETF批准预期驱动。 5. ETF资金流未证实通过增加周一交易量来放大效应，机制仍存疑。
Cryptocurrencies trade continuously while major traditional markets close over the weekend. We examine whether weekend cryptocurrency volatility predicts Monday variance in equity, commodity and fixed-income markets. Using daily range-based variance measures for Bitcoin, Ether, XRP, the S&P 500, gold and a US Treasury ETF over 2017-2026, we augment heterogeneous autoregressive models with a common weekend cryptocurrency factor. Predictive content is weak before 2024 but significant thereafter. In the post-2024 sample, a one-standard-deviation increase in the factor is associated with 27-54% higher fitted Monday variance. Adding the factor reduces out-of-sample QLIKE losses by 11-22%, although statistical evidence varies across markets. Friday cryptocurrency volatility does not reproduce the result, and coin-specific variation adds no significant predictive information beyond the common factor. An endogenous procedure estimates a break in late 2023, during growing anticipation of US spot-Bitcoin ETF approval. However, ETF-flow interactions provide no evidence of amplification through greater measured Monday flow activity, leaving the mechanism unresolved. The findings suggest that calendar-specific volatility measures reveal predictive information that aggregate connectedness measures may obscure. arXiv categories: q-fin.ST

item.title: What Prediction-Market Contracts Reveal at Launch: Trading Volume and Dispute Risk
item.content:encoded:
Polymarket, 交易量预测, 争议预测, 平台变更, 特征解释

总结: 基于Polymarket近80万市场数据，利用合约元数据预测交易量与争议。交易量预测表现优异，市场话题贡献最大，神经网络提升有限。然而，平台变更导致模型失效，主要因新问题形式未在训练集中，且供需关系发生转变。争议预测较稳定但精准度低，适合市场排序，不适合个别预测。
arXiv:2610.29578v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using a near-census of 802,863 resolved markets listed on Polymarket between January 2023 and May 2026, and only information available at listing (the market's title and description, named resolution source, and contract metadata), we predict lifetime trading volume and whether settlement is later disputed. Contract information predicts trading volume well (out-of-sample $R^2 = 0.747$ for log volume), and most of the signal is interpretable: market topic provides the largest gain ($+0.289$ $R^2$ over a $0.220$ contract-feature baseline), wording and resolution-rule design add smaller but measurable improvements ($+0.027$ combined), and neural text models add little beyond the interpretable features. This performance does not survive a period of platform change coinciding with a shift in listing formats: accuracy in predicting whether a market reaches \$1,000 falls from AUC $0.940$ under same-period evaluation to $0.577$ when training on past quarters and testing on later ones. The loss concentrates in markets whose question forms were absent from training (76.9% of test markets; on familiar forms the model still reaches $0.778$), and a decomposition attributes more of it to a changed relationship between contract characteristics and demand than to an outdated mapping from text to features. Dispute predictors are more stable but less precise: launch-time features rank dispute risk far better than chance (AUC $0.78$), yet at a 0.31% base rate precision is too low for case-by-case prediction (average precision $0.012$), so the scores suit ranking groups of markets rather than forecasting individual disputes.

item.title: GROMM: Generative Risk-neutral Option Market Models
item.content:encoded:
无套利，欧洲期权，局部波动率，SANOS 框架，平滑插值

总结: 本文提出基于SANOS框架的静态和动态无套利欧洲期权市场模型，具备平滑插值功能，并证明其动态过程存在唯一强解。该模型将局部波动率视为价格曲面表示而非定价模型。研究利用S&P指数期权数据，显示模型初始状态拟合买卖价差超95%。在$\mathbb{P}$和$\mathbb{Q}$下训练后，验证了模型的无套利特性及对市场动态的良好拟合，并提出BHW测试以检验无套利。
arXiv:2610.16732v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a statically and dynamically arbitrage-free European option market model with smooth interpolation between option prices, based on the SANOS framework, and prove that its dynamics admit a unique strong solution. In spirit, it is a stochastic model for local volatility when the latter is used as a representation of a European option price surface, not as a pricing model. We illustrate the strength of our approach on S&P Index Option data from January 2022 to August 2025. We show that the model's initial state fits within bid/ask for more than 95% of relevant market option prices. We then train the model dynamics under $\mathbb{P}$ and $\mathbb{Q}$ and show that the model is indeed free of arbitrage while fitting the dynamics of the market well. We also propose a range of BHW-tests to test for absence of arbitrage.

item.title: More Mentions, Less Information? Diagnosing Identity and Alignment in Reddit Embeddings for Volatility Forecasting
item.content:encoded: <div> arXiv:2610.25468v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Since the 2021 GameStop short squeeze, r/WallStreetBets (WSB) has been associated with episodes of extreme volatility, and its text is increasingly used to forecast volatility. A model using only large language model (LLM) embeddings of WSB posts attains an out-of-sample $R^2$ of 0.13 for log realized variance. That number shows predictive power, but it does not reveal where the information comes from or how much the text adds beyond a firm's own volatility history. We answer these questions with a diagnostic protocol that nests embeddings on a heterogeneous autoregressive (HAR) benchmark, compares them with text-free firm-identity controls, shuffles the day-to-text pairing within firm-years to test day-specific alignment, and checks whether gains persist across periods and coverage groups. We apply the protocol to frozen LLM embeddings in a panel of 202,145 mentioned stock-days, using retrospective rolling out-of-sample tests over 2015-2022. The results indicate that most of the standalone fit reflects firm or firm-year information: on firms seen in training, a text-free firm baseline reaches $R^2 = 0.32$, shuffling preserves 89-92% of the standalone fit, and masking ticker strings reduces standalone $R^2$ to -0.005. Adding embeddings to HAR reduces equal-date MSE by 1.22% (95% CI [0.94, 1.49]). This small but statistically significant gain survives firm controls and ticker masking, but is largely eliminated by alignment shuffling. The gain is concentrated in 2015-2019 and is not distinguishable from zero in 2020-2022. Expanding coverage by 48% through off-hours and weekend posts adds stock-days with no reliable positive increment. More mentions therefore do not imply more incremental forecasting information. <div> arXiv:2610.25468v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Since the 2021 GameStop short squeeze, r/WallStreetBets (WSB) has been associated with episodes of extreme volatility, and its text is increasingly used to forecast volatility. item.title: Conflicting History in Foundation Model Return Forecasts
item.content:encoded: <div> arXiv:2610.25822v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Older observations can help a forecaster learn a predictive relationship while becoming misleading when that relationship changes. We study this tension using paired return histories that differ in older observations but share recent returns and the conditional distribution of the next return. Across five foundation-model forecasting procedures and three simulated processes, each evaluated on 1,024 independent replications, conflicting history reduces the probability of improving on zero in all 30 higher-signal comparisons. This loss of usefulness occurs despite successful signal recovery under stable conditions. A separate exploratory comparison on 56 assets finds that shortening inputs from 256 to 64 returns increases mean absolute error for every model by 1.77-4.58 basis points; neither length improves observed overall error over zero. The evidence distinguishes the ability to extract a signal from the ability to withstand conflicting history, while showing why context sensitivity alone does not justify discarding older data. <div> arXiv:2610.25822v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Older observations can help a forecaster learn a predictive relationship while becoming misleading when that relationship changes. item.title: Amortized Neural Filtering for Calibrated Posteriors in Statistical Arbitrage
item.content:encoded: <div> arXiv:2610.25802v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Statistical arbitrage trades on an estimate of the state of a residual spread, and conventional practice discards the uncertainty of that estimate. We keep the uncertainty and use it in the trading decision. A Neural Filter Estimator (NFE) is trained on simulated paths of a mean-reverting process whose innovation law is selected by testing candidates against real residuals; once trained, it returns the posterior over the latent state of every spread in a cross-section in one forward pass. Three results follow. On simulated paths with known truth, every practical estimator, ours included, falls in one narrow band of accuracy well below an estimator given full information, so the posterior gains no accuracy over a point estimate; its contribution is a correct account of its own uncertainty. On Korean equities, net of costs, the conventional point estimate forecasts about a thousand basis points per holding period more than it realizes, and the amortized methods cut that gap by a factor of roughly two to eight. Sizing positions from the posterior on the same learned factors as the end-to-end Attention Factor Model matches the Sharpe ratio of those factors under the base rule within the period's noise, at no more risk. <div> arXiv:2610.25802v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Statistical arbitrage trades on an estimate of the state of a residual spread, and conventional practice discards the uncertainty of that estimate. item.title: Probability-Weighting Functions for Normal Tempered-Stable Laws: Orthogonal Channels and Information-Theoretic Indices
item.content:encoded: <div> arXiv:2610.26746v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A probability-weighting function (PWF) maps objective probabilities into decision weights. We construct PWFs from changes in the distribution of returns rather than from a parametric family: with prior and posterior return distributions $F_{prior}$ and $F_{post}$, the PWF is $w(p) = F_{post}(F_{prior}^{-1}(p))$. Both distributions are normal tempered-stable (NTS), and the posterior differs from the prior along one of three channels, each isolated with the variance held fixed: scale, skewness and tail thickness. Around a symmetric benchmark with excess kurtosis 3, a 40% change in scale moves cumulative probabilities by up to 7 to 8 percentage points, a skewness of $\pm 0.5$ by 2 percentage points, and a change of $\pm 0.3$ in the tail index by about 2 percentage points. The three channels leave distinct signatures: the deviation $w(p) - p$ changes sign once, twice and three times, respectively. Three information-theoretic indices (a Fisher-normalized logit shift, a signed Jensen-Shannon divergence and a log-odds elasticity) summarize the distortions and avoid the endpoint singularity of the classical ratio $(w(p)-p)/[p(1-p)]$. Applied to NTS parameters calibrated to S&P 500 ETF daily returns over 2015-2025, the same channels produce distortions of 2 to 7 percentage points. Code that reproduces every figure and number in the paper is provided. <div> arXiv:2610.26746v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A probability-weighting function (PWF) maps objective probabilities into decision weights. item.title: Market Efficiency in a Changing Asset Population: Mobility, Entry, and Survival over Cryptocurrency's Full History
item.content:encoded: <div> arXiv:2610.23283v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Weak-form efficiency implies symmetry restrictions on the Markov chain governing movement across the cryptocurrency capitalisation distribution. We test them on the full listed population: 8,970 assets, 690 weekly cross-sections, 2013 to 2026, with entry, exit and survival observed rather than inferred. Symmetry is rejected in every era, but the asymmetry falls by seventy percent, and what converged is entry-driven compositional churn rather than coins' own valuations. The bottom decile earns 27.5% per week on paper and nothing among assets that trade, on capacity of $293,000. Compensation for neglect exists precisely where trading does not. <div> arXiv:2610.23283v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Weak-form efficiency implies symmetry restrictions on the Markov chain governing movement across the cryptocurrency capitalisation distribution. item.title: Conditionally Identifiable Latent Representation for Multivariate Time Series with Structural Dynamics
item.content:encoded: <div> arXiv:2603.22886v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose the Identifiable Variational Dynamic Factor Model (iVDFM) for multivariate time series. The model combines variational inference with partial identifiability guarantees up to a known ambiguity class. Innovations follow a conditional exponential-family prior over observed auxiliary context and regime embeddings. Linear diagonal dynamics map innovations to factors and preserve that class, so factors are partially identifiable up to permutation and component-wise affine maps. We train by maximizing the ELBO and estimate uncertainty in both latent trajectories and forecasts. Under explicit assumptions, we prove partial identifiability up to the stated class and provide the full proof in the appendix. We evaluate factor recovery on synthetic DGPs, intervention behavior on synthetic SCMs, and forecasting on real benchmarks with CRPS and MSE. <div> arXiv:2603.22886v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose the Identifiable Variational Dynamic Factor Model (iVDFM) for multivariate time series. item.title: Buy the Rumor, Sell the News: When Is News Priced In?
item.content:encoded: <div> arXiv:2608.14014v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Two old market sayings hold that news is already priced in by the time it is published, and that the rumor is bought while the news is sold. Both are empirical claims about event time: they place the price move associated with a piece of news before and at publication rather than after it. Whether the claims hold, for which kinds of news, and by how much are basic questions about how fast markets absorb public information. We test them on 4.57 million financial news articles covering roughly 3,000 US stocks (2023-2026). A large language model teacher, distilled into a compact classifier through active learning, assigns each article one of 17 event tags and five attributes; articles are clustered into stories to separate first reports from follow-up coverage; and beta-adjusted abnormal returns are measured around the resulting 1.68 million stock-day events, with 364{,}405 neutral-sentiment events as a placebo group. Three results follow.
